To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the expression of several genes is associated with the noncytotoxic, anti-HIV CD8+ cell response.

the gene expression profiles of the CD8+ noncytotoxic antiviral cells are distinct from those of cytotoxic CD8+ cells and that these profiles are also distinct from those of CD8+ T cells from HIV-positive subjects who lack the noncytotoxic activity.
we have identified three genes that are associated with the noncytotoxic, antiviral activity of CD8+ T cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of genes expressed in HIV-specific CD8+ T cells that are involved in the antiviral activity of these cells.
identifying the genes associated with the noncytotoxic antiviral activity of CD8+ T cells in HIV infection.
identifying genes associated with the CD4-independent, noncytotoxic, anti-HIV activity exhibited by CD8+ lymphocytes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CD8+ suppressive cells from the HIV-1-infected twin had a unique gene expression profile that was not found in any of the other HIV-infected subjects.
CD8+ cells that suppress HIV replication have a distinct gene expression profile compared to CD8+ cells without this antiviral property.
CD8+ noncytotoxic cells from HIV-infected individuals with a noncytotoxic response to HIV-1 have increased gene expression of a number of genes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

CD8+ T cells from HIV-infected individuals with noncytotoxic, antiviral activity have a gene expression pattern that differs from those CD8+ cells without antiviral activity, and that this gene expression pattern can be detected in the CD8 cells of HIV-infected individuals.
we have identified a gene expression pattern that is associated with CD8+ noncytotoxic antiviral activity and have confirmed that this pattern is evident in other individuals.
CD8+ cell-mediated inhibition of HIV replication is associated with a distinct pattern of gene expression.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a unique gene expression profile associated with antiviral CD4+ and CD8+ cells that is different from cells that do not have this activity.
we have identified a gene that is expressed at a higher level in the CD8 cells from HIV positive patients who exhibit this antiviral response.
we have identified three genes that are differentially expressed in CD8+ lymphocytes that exhibit antiviral activity, and these may play a role in HIV suppression.
